english.title: Religious hatred - distribute recording of threatening visual images / sounds intending to stir up
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) distributed a recording of visual images or sounds, namely **(..SPECIFY THE RECORDING..), which were threatening, intending thereby to stir up religious hatred
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 29E(1) and 29L(3) of the Public Order Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording is now OBSOLETE. Now see CJS Code PU86141 and H6663. Option re "Sexual orientation" added by Sch 16 to the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 as from 23/03/2010.

(i) Section 29E(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that recording means any record from which visual images or sounds may, by any means, be reproduced; and references to the distribution of a recording are to its distribution to the public or a section of the public.
(ii) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution of this offence.
(iii) See also H8427 'show/play recording of threatening images/sounds intending to stir up religious hatred'.
(iv) Section 29L(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that for purposes of the rules in England and Wales against charging more than one offence in the same count or information, each of sections 29B to 29G creates one offence.
(v) This offence was inserted into the Public Order Act 1986 by the Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.
